title: Failover types
content:
## Overview

FortiGate HA provides multiple types of failover protection to ensure that a secondary device can take over when the primary experiences a problem. Understanding the different failover types helps you design a resilient HA deployment and configure the right monitoring options for your environment.

![Failover types](diagram:0)

## Common Failover Types

**Device failover** occurs when the secondary devices stop receiving hello packets from the primary FortiGate. This indicates the primary is no longer reachable.

**Link failover** occurs when the link status of a monitored interface on the primary FortiGate goes down. You can configure the HA cluster to monitor one or more interfaces. If a monitored interface on the primary is unplugged or its link status goes down, a new primary FortiGate is elected.

**Remote link failover** uses the link health monitor feature to monitor the health of one or more interfaces against one or more servers that act as beacons. The primary FortiGate fails over if the accumulated penalty of all failed interfaces reaches the configured threshold.

**Memory-based failover**: triggered when memory utilization on the primary FortiGate reaches the configured threshold for the configured monitoring period.

**SSD failover**: triggers a failover if FortiOS detects Ext-fs errors on an SSD on the primary FortiGate.

## Failover Trigger Events

Multiple events can trigger an HA failover:

- Hardware or software failure on the primary FortiGate
- An issue on one of the interfaces on the primary
- An administrator-triggered failover

When a failover occurs, an event log is generated. Optionally, you can configure the device to also generate SNMP traps and alert emails.

## Session Pickup

Enabling session pickup allows active sessions to be seamlessly picked up by the new primary in the event of an HA failover. Users' sessions continue uninterrupted, and they will not notice that a failover occurred.

Note that there are limitations: sessions that terminate at the FortiGate itself — such as SSL VPN sessions and proxy sessions — cannot be handed off to another FortiGate and must be restarted on the new primary.

## Virtual MAC Addresses

To forward traffic correctly after a failover, a FortiGate HA solution uses virtual MAC addresses. When a primary joins an HA cluster, each interface is assigned a virtual MAC address based on the HA group ID, virtual cluster ID (if enabled), and interface index number.

Key behaviors:

- If two or more HA clusters are in the same broadcast domain with the same HA group ID, MAC address conflicts may occur — assign different HA group IDs to each cluster
- Upon failover, the new primary adopts the same virtual MAC addresses for the equivalent interfaces
- The new primary broadcasts gratuitous ARP packets, notifying the network that each virtual MAC address is now reachable through a different switch port
- The reserved HA management interface keeps its original MAC address and is NOT assigned a virtual MAC address

> **Key terms:** A configuration backup completion can trigger a failover test in some HA test scenarios.

questionPool.question: What triggers a device failover in a FortiGate HA cluster?
choices: A link status change on a monitored interface
The secondary devices stop receiving hello packets from the primary
Memory utilization exceeds the configured threshold
An SSD error is detected on the primary
questionPool.explanation: A device failover occurs when the secondary devices stop receiving hello packets from the primary FortiGate, indicating the primary is no longer reachable.

questionPool.question: What triggers a link failover?
choices: The primary FortiGate stops sending hello packets
The link status of a monitored interface on the primary FortiGate goes down
Memory utilization reaches a threshold
A remote server stops responding to probes
questionPool.explanation: A link failover occurs when the link status of a monitored interface on the primary FortiGate goes down. If a monitored interface is unplugged or its link status goes down, a new primary FortiGate is elected.

questionPool.question: What feature is used for remote link failover monitoring?
choices: SNMP polling
The link health monitor feature, which monitors interfaces against beacon servers
DPD (Dead Peer Detection)
BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection)
questionPool.explanation: When you configure remote link failover, FortiGate uses the link health monitor feature to monitor the health of one or more interfaces against one or more servers that act as beacons.

questionPool.question: What triggers memory-based failover?
choices: Memory errors detected on the primary
Memory utilization on the primary reaches the configured threshold for the configured monitoring period
RAM modules become faulty on the primary
Memory synchronization between cluster members fails
questionPool.explanation: If you enable memory-based failover, an HA failover is triggered when the memory utilization on the primary FortiGate reaches the configured threshold for the configured monitoring period.

questionPool.question: What triggers SSD failover?
choices: SSD utilization exceeds 90%
FortiOS detects Ext-fs errors on an SSD on the primary FortiGate
The SSD reaches end-of-life based on write cycles
The SSD synchronization with the secondary fails
questionPool.explanation: You can also enable SSD failover, which triggers a failover if FortiOS detects Ext-fs errors on an SSD on the primary FortiGate.

questionPool.question: What is generated when a failover occurs?
choices: Only an SNMP trap
Only an alert email
An event log is generated, and optionally SNMP traps and alert emails
A syslog entry only
questionPool.explanation: When a failover occurs, an event log is generated. Optionally, you can configure the device to also generate SNMP traps and alert emails.

questionPool.question: What does enabling session pickup allow in the event of an HA failover?
choices: Active sessions are dropped and immediately re-established faster
Active sessions are seamlessly picked up by the new primary, continuing uninterrupted
Only new sessions are allowed after failover
Session pickup forces all sessions to the backup ISP
questionPool.explanation: Enabling session pickup allows active sessions to be seamlessly picked up by the new primary in the event of an HA failover. Users' sessions continue uninterrupted, and they will not even know that a failover occurred.

questionPool.question: Which type of sessions CANNOT be handed off to the new primary during a failover?
choices: TCP sessions with SNAT
HTTP sessions through a firewall policy
Sessions that terminate at the FortiGate itself, such as SSL VPN and proxy sessions
UDP sessions
questionPool.explanation: Sessions that terminate at the FortiGate itself — such as SSL VPN sessions and proxy sessions — cannot be handed off to another FortiGate and must be restarted on the new primary.

questionPool.question: What are virtual MAC addresses based on in a FortiGate HA cluster?
choices: The IP address of each interface
The HA group ID, virtual cluster ID (if enabled), and interface index number
The serial number of the primary FortiGate
The physical MAC address of the primary
questionPool.explanation: When a primary joins an HA cluster, each interface is assigned a virtual MAC address. The HA group ID, virtual cluster ID (if enabled), and interface index number are used in the creation of virtual MAC addresses.

questionPool.question: What should you do if two HA clusters are in the same broadcast domain to avoid MAC address conflicts?
choices: Use different firmware versions
Assign different HA group IDs to each cluster
Use different heartbeat interface speeds
Configure different priority values on each cluster
questionPool.explanation: If you have two or more HA clusters in the same broadcast domain using the same HA group ID, you might get MAC address conflicts. It is strongly recommended that you assign different HA group IDs to each cluster.

questionPool.question: How does the network learn that a virtual MAC address is now reachable through a different switch port after failover?
choices: The new primary sends an SNMP notification
The new primary broadcasts gratuitous ARP packets
The secondary sends updated routing tables via OSPF
The cluster administrator must manually update ARP tables
questionPool.explanation: Upon failover, the new primary broadcasts gratuitous ARP packets, notifying the network that each virtual MAC address is now reachable through a different switch port.

questionPool.question: What happens to the MAC address of the reserved HA management interface during failover?
choices: It adopts the same virtual MAC address as the primary
It keeps its original MAC address and is not changed to a virtual MAC address
It gets a randomly generated MAC address
It uses the MAC address of the new primary
questionPool.explanation: The MAC address of a reserved HA management interface is not changed to a virtual MAC address. Instead, the reserved management interface keeps its original MAC address.

questionPool.question: What does the new primary do with virtual MAC addresses upon failover?
choices: It generates new virtual MAC addresses for all interfaces
It adopts the same virtual MAC addresses for the equivalent interfaces as the previous primary
It reverts to its hardware MAC addresses
It uses DHCP to obtain new MAC assignments
questionPool.explanation: Upon failover, a secondary adopts the same virtual MAC addresses for the equivalent interfaces. The new primary then broadcasts gratuitous ARP packets to update the network.

questionPool.question: What determines whether a remote link failover is triggered?
choices: A single interface failure always triggers failover
The accumulated penalty of all failed interfaces reaches the configured threshold
Any link going down to a beacon server triggers failover
Only if all monitored links are down
questionPool.explanation: The primary FortiGate fails over if the accumulated penalty of all failed interfaces reaches the configured threshold when using remote link failover.

questionPool.question: Which of the following is NOT a common HA failover trigger?
choices: Hardware or software failure on the primary
An issue on one of the interfaces on the primary
An administrator-triggered failover
A configuration backup completion
questionPool.explanation: Common HA failover triggers include hardware or software failure on the primary, an issue on one of the interfaces on the primary, and an administrator-triggered failover. A configuration backup completion is not a failover trigger.
